title: BA1/1381/2023 of PULKIT ARYA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
1st Bail Application No. 1381 of 2023
Pulkit Arya ........Applicant

Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Aditya Singh, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. G.S. Sandhu, Government Advocate assisted by Ms. Manisha Rana
Singh, AGA for the State.
Mr. Navnish Negi, Advocate for the father of the deceased.

Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Applicant Pulkit Arya is in judicial custody in
FIR No. 1 of 2022 dated 20.09.2022, under Sections 302,
201, 354-A, 120-B IPC and Section 5(1)(b) of the Immoral
Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, P.S./Patti Udaypur Palla-2,
Pauri Garhwal. He has sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. The prosecution case, as unfolded, is as
follows; the applicant owns a resort far from the city area.
The deceased, a young girl, who had completed Class 12th
in the year 2020 had secured a job of receptionist in the
resort. She was found missing from there. It is the
applicant, who first lodged the FIR in the matter with the
averments that the deceased was under tremendous
tension due to certain reasons. The applicant wanted to

2
speak to her father, therefore, he asked the telephone
number of the father of the deceased. Due to this, the
deceased was further troubled. Since the deceased was
fond of outing, the applicant asked one of his colleagues
to take the deceased out from the resort, but at the
instance of the colleague, the applicant also joined them.
They took 2 two-wheelers and returned at the resort.
Next day morning, according to the FIR, the applicant was
told that the deceased was not in her room. During
investigation, it was revealed that, in fact, the applicant
and the co-accused were molesting the deceased in the
resort; they were pestering her for immoral activities; they
were pressurising her to give extra services to the guests,
to which the deceased was not agreeable. The applicant
and the co-accused had a sense of fear that perhaps the
deceased might reveal it to others. Therefore, according to
the prosecution, on 18.09.2022, the applicant along with
the co-accused took the deceased out from the resort.
They killed her and threw her in a canal. The dead body
was recovered on 24.09.2022.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that there are no CCTV footages. The resort was
destroyed and the DVR was damaged. He would also raise
the following points in his submission:-

3
(i) The friend of the deceased had visited her
on 15.09.2022 and he stayed there till
17.07.2022; some most personal used
articles were found in her room, which
were brought to the notice of the
applicant.
(ii) The applicant was disturbed for that
reason. The applicant wanted to speak to
the father of the deceased, therefore, she
became more perturbed.
(iii) The applicant had asked one of his
colleagues to take her out for walk, but on
their instance, the applicant also joined
them. They all had returned to the resort.
(iv) The witnesses were called by the police on
19.09.2022, prior to lodging of the FIR.
They were not allowed to meet anyone.
(v) PW 24 Chandrakiran Bharti was
examined at trial. He has admitted in para
13 of his statement that he had seen the
deceased in the resort after their return
on 18.09.2022.

4
(vi) PW 29 Yashpal Singh Bisht, the Engineer
of the Power House, has stated that the
time of taking out the dead body from the
boat is prior to the time when the boat
reached at the spot. It is argued that even
it is a case of planted dead body.
(vii) It is not stated by any of the witnesses
that he has not seen the deceased in her
room on 18.09.2022. The witnesses have
improvised their statement at trial. They
have stated during trial, what they have
not stated during investigation, even
under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973.
(viii) Material witnesses have already been
examined. There is no chance of
tampering with the evidence.
(ix) The applicant has a deep root in the
society. There are no chances of fleeing
from justice.
(x) There is no such evidence, which may
deny bail to the applicant.

5
5. Learned counsel appearing for the father of the
deceased would submit that much before the FIR was
lodged, when the father of the deceased approached the
applicant, he had stated that the CCTVs in his resort
were not in the working order. The applicant never
informed the informant that the deceased was missing.
He would raise the following points as well in his
submission:-
(i) PW 23 Pushpdeep Baboria, who is friend
of the deceased, had telephonic
conversation with the deceased that she
was along with the applicant and the co-accused. She apprehended that anything
might happen to her, thereafter, she was
not traceable.
(ii) PW 9 Aman Rai, in paras 4 and 5 of the
statement before the Court, has stated
that, in fact, he was persuaded by the
applicant and the co-accused to
manufacture false evidence and tell that
he had seen the deceased in her room of
the resort in the night of 18.09.2022.

6
(iii) PW 7 Kushraj has stated that, in fact, the
applicant had been molesting the
deceased.
6. Learned State Counsel would submit that the
crime scene was protected in the instant case; PW 18
Sandhya Negi had visited the crime scene and a forensic
team had also inspected it. She would submit that the
investigation was transferred to the regular police.
7. Learned State Counsel would also submit that
there are circumstances, which prove that it is the
applicant and the co-accused, who killed the deceased.
She would submit that PW 6 Abhinav Kashyap and PW 7
Khushraj had stated that they have seen that on the
18.09.2022, four persons left the resort, including the
applicant, but the deceased did not return. PW 14 SI
Omkant Bhushan, who has studied the telephonic
location, has confirmed that the deceased was along with
the applicant and the co-accused, but suddenly she
disappeared from the place, near to which her dead body
was found from a canal.
8. Learned State Counsel would also submit that :
(i) PW 8 Vivek Arya and PW 13 Ayush Kumar
also stated that on 18.09.2022, in the

7
evening, the deceased was much
perturbed; she wanted to leave the resort;
she was crying.
(ii) PW 15 Dr. Ravi Prakash Mishra and PW
16 Dr. Ashish Ramesh Bhute have
confirmed that the deceased did not die
due to accidental slip, instead she was
thrown into the canal.
9. Learned State Counsel would argue that the
conduct of the applicant proves that it is not a case for
bail. Witnesses were pressurized to make statement that
the deceased had returned in the resort on 18.09.2022.
10. It is a stage of bail. Much of the discussion is
not expected of. The discussion is being made with the
caveat that any observation made in this order shall not
have any bearing at the trial.
11. Definitely, it is a case based on circumstantial
evidence. The evidence has been read over to a certain
extent. This Court refrains to make deeper scrutiny of the
statements, but the fact remains that PW 6 Abhinav
Kashyap and PW 7 Khushraj have seen that in the
evening of 18.09.2022, the applicant along with the co-accused and the deceased had left the resort. In fact, PW

8
6 Abhinav Kashyap has also stated that when, for the
first time, in the evening, he saw the deceased, the
applicant was in her room. The deceased was crying that
she should be taken out from the resort, but the
applicant snatched the mobile phone of the deceased and
pulled her inside the room. These witnesses have stated
that, thereafter, the deceased did not return. They did not
see her. When the meal was to be served, the applicant
and the co-accused stopped him to take the meal in the
room of the deceased.
12. PW 10 Saurab Bisht and PW 12 Manveer Singh
Chauhan have also stated that they have not seen the
deceased back in the resort. In fact, they have stated that
they were not permitted to take meal in the room of the
deceased.
13. PW 23 Pushpadeep Baboria has categorically
stated as to what happened on 18.09.2022. He has stated
that the deceased was much uncomfortable because she
was being molested in the resort; she was being pestered
for immoral activities in the resort, which she was
denying.
14. There are WhatsApp chats on the record,
although before the trial court it has to be proved in

9
accordance with law. PW 23 Pushpadeep Baboria has
been cross-examined on this aspect. These WhatsApp
chats reveal as if the deceased was, in fact, pressurized.
She was in tremendous trauma. In one of her chats on
17.09.2022, it is written at 09:38 p.m. "Esa hki VIP
guest arhe h." Thereafter at 09:38 p.m., on the same day,
she again texted "Th unhe extra service chaiy.". Same
day again, at 09:42 p.m. she texted to Pushpadeep "Mene
bola bhai tu kya sochta ki m gareeb hu th y 10 k m
bhik jau.". At 09:48 p.m., she again writes "Rand bnane
me tule h."
15. PW 23 Pushpadeep Baboria did speak to the
deceased at 08:32 p.m. on 18.09.2022, therefore, her
phone was switched off. PW 14 SI Omkant Bhushan has
confirmed that from her location, the telephone of the
deceased was not traceable. It is near the place of the
incidence.
16. PW 8 Vivek Arya and PW 13 Ayush Kumar both
have stated that on 11.09.2022, the applicant had kissed
her. She was being pressurized to give extra services.
17. PW 1, the father of the deceased, has stated
that on 20.09.2022, he had questioned the applicant

10
about CCTV footages and he was told that they are not in
order.
18. PW 15 Dr. Ravi Prakash Mishra and PW 16 Dr.
Ashish Ramesh Bhute have quite extensively stated that
the death of the deceased was not by accidental slip.
19. PW 9 Aman Rai has, in paras 4 an 5 of the
statement, stated that he was persuaded by the co-accused to give false statement that the deceased had
returned.
20. A young girl was molested; she was pressurized
to undergo immoral activities in the resort; she was
pressurized to give extra services; her trauma is reflected
in WhatsApp texts sent to PW 23 Pushpadeep Baboria
and according to the prosecution, under a design to
eliminate her, she has been killed.
21. Having considered the gravity of offence and all
other attending factors, this Court is of the view that it is
not a case fit for bail. Accordingly, the bail application
deserves to be rejected.
22. The bail application is rejected.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J)
20.12.2023
Avneet/
